PRE-DEMOLITION COMMENCEMENTPlanning PhasingThe development shall be phased for planning purposes in accordance with
the Illustrative Phasing Plan (6699-SRA-ZZ-ZZ-DR-A-02155
Rev P02) hereby approved, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local
Planning Authority.

Demolition DEMPNo demolition shall take place on any phase or building (as appropriate)
until a Demolition Environmental Management Plan (DEMP) has been submitted to,
and approved in writing, by the local planning authority.The DEMP shall set out, as a minimum:(a) a protected species survey;(b) a method statement detailing how any protected species will be
protected during demolition; (c) details of demolition lighting;The works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved DEMP, or
any amendment or variation to it as may be agreed in writing by the local
planning authority throughout the demolition period.This is a PRE-COMMENCEMENT Condition.

Invasive Species Prior to the commencement of any phase of development (excluding
demolition and site clearance, but including groundworks), an Invasive
Non-Native Species Management Plan (INNSMP) detailing the strategy for the
containment, control, treatment, and/or eradication of all identified Invasive
Non-Native Species (INNS) on the site, shall be submitted and approved in
writing by the local planning authority. The development shall be carried out in full accordance with the
approved INNSMP, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning
Authority and Natural England (or any other relevant body).

Demolition and Construction Site Waste Management Plan Prior to any phase of demolition works relating to the
Detailed Application, or applications for approval of Reserved Matters for each
relevant phase relating to access, appearance, landscaping layout and scale submitted
pursuant to this permission shall be accompanied by a Site Waste Management
Plan (SWMP), in compliance with Best Practice Standards.  This document shall explain:(a) how the
requirement to recover at least 70% (by volume) of   construction and demolition waste from landfill is to be met;(b) how
demolition and excavation materials will be re-used or recycled as appropriate;(c) the
arrangements for storage of materials to be recycled or re-used;(d) how
materials are procured from sustainable sources wherever possible; and(e) the
designation of a 'Waste Champion', who will seek to minimise    over-ordering and material spoilage, as well
as ensuring the effectiveness of
waste segregation.The Site Waste Management Plan shall be implemented as
approved.

Circular Economy Post Construction monitoringPrior to the occupation of each relevant Phase or Block of the Detailed
Application and Outline Application, a post construction monitoring report
should be completed in line with the GLA’s Circular Economy Statement Guidance.
The report should be submitted to and approved by the LPA in writing.

Nesting birdsSite clearance, demolition, other such
preparation works and construction of all phases shall be either undertaken
outside of the bird nesting season, or if this cannot be avoided, a nesting
bird check by an appropriately qualified ecologist shall be carried out prior
to works commencing. If an active nest is discovered, then an appropriate
species-dependant exclusion zone should be enacted, whereby all works within an
appropriate buffer zone (as defined by the ecologist) should be prevented until
the young birds have fledged and/or the nest is no longer active.

Construction Environment Management Plan (CEMP)No development within each phase or building (other than demolition in
accordance with the approved Demolition Environment Management Plan) shall take
place, until a Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) has been
submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The
CEMP shall set out, as a minimum:(a)     details of construction lighting;(b)     any permanent fixtures to be included as part of the final
development to preserve or mitigate the disruption of protected species
habitats or passageways. The works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved CEMP, or
any amendment or variation to it as may be agreed in writing by the local
planning authority throughout the construction period.

Foundation DesignThe development hereby
approved shall not commence in any phase (other than in relation to site
demolition, clearance and site preparation works) until details of foundation
design to take account of existing trees to be retained and surrounding the
site (and as recommended by the Arboricultural Report submitted by Sharon
Hosegood Associates, Dated July 2025) have been submitted to and approved in
writing by the local planning authority. The development shall thereafter take
place in accordance with the approved details.

London

hereby permitted shall not be commenced on any relevant phase or block
(excluding demolition and site clearance works) until the following documents,
in consultation with TfL Infrastructure Protection, have been submitted to and
approved in writing by the local planning authority which: 1.   
provide
detailed design and Risk Assessment Method Statement on the use of scaffold and
tall plant i.e tower cranes and lifting equipment;2.   
demonstrate
that the train driver’s vision will not be disturbed or impaired by the

satisfaction;3.   
an
assessment of railway noise and vibration shall be carried out and appropriate
protective measures shall be taken to protect the users of the property and of
other properties potentially affected as a result of the current development
against noise and vibration.

Landscaping ImplementationAll planting,
seeding or turfing comprised in the approved details of landscaping within the
Detailed phase of the Development or the Outline Phase of the Development shall
be carried out in the first planting and seeding seasons following the
occupation of the building(s), or the completion of the development, whichever
is the sooner.  Any existing or new trees
or shrubs which, within a period of 5 years from the completion of the
development, die, are removed, or become seriously damaged or diseased, shall
be replaced in the next planting season, with others of a similar size and
species, unless the local authority agrees any variation in writing.

CONSTRUCTIONReporting of unexpected contamination Any contamination that is found during the
course of construction of any phase of the development hereby permitted
(inclusive of both the Detailed Application and the Outline Application) that
was not previously identified shall be reported immediately to the local
planning authority. Development on the part of the site affected shall be
suspended until a risk assessment has been carried out and submitted to and
approved in writing by the local planning authority. Where unacceptable risks
are found, the development [or relevant phase of development] shall not resume
or continue until remediation and verification schemes have been carried out in
accordance with details that shall first have been submitted to and approved in
writing by the local planning authority.

Piling No piling shall take place on any
phase until a PILING METHOD STATEMENT (detailing the depth and type of piling
to be undertaken and the methodology by which such piling will be carried out,
including measures to prevent and minimise the potential for damage to
subsurface sewerage infrastructure, and the programme for the works) and piling
layout plan including all Thames Water wastewater assets, the local topography
and clearance between the face of the pile to the face of a pipe has been
submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority in
consultation with Thames Water.Any piling must be undertaken in
accordance with the terms of the approved piling method statement and piling
layout plan.

No Works Below Chalk Aquifer No works involving excavations on
any phase below the chalk groundwater table shall take place (for example,
piling or the implementation of a geothermal open/closed loop system), until a
ground investigation has first been carried out to identify appropriate
techniques and to avoid displacing any shallow contamination to a greater
depth, which could impact the chalk aquifer. A ground investigation report
shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority in
consultation with Affinity Water, prior to such works commencing.

Air Quality The development hereby approved
shall be carried out in full accordance with the recommendations contained
within the Air Quality Assessment (prepared by Phlorum, Chapter 9 of the
Environment Statement and associated addendum and appendices). The
recommendations contained within the assessment shall be implemented and
maintained for the period that such works are being undertaken.

Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM)All Non-Road Mobile Machinery
(NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the
course of the demolition, site preparation and construction phases shall comply
with the emission standards as published on the NRMM Website (https://nrmm.london/).
Unless it complies with the standards set out on the website, no NRMM shall be
on site, at any time, whether in use or not, without the prior written consent
of the local planning authority. The developer shall keep an up to date list of
all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases
of the development on the online register at https:// nrmm.london/

GROUND LEVELLevels to be ApprovedThe development hereby permitted in relation to
the Detailed Application or the Outline Application shall not progress above
ground in each relevant phase until details of the levels of the building(s),
road(s) and footpath(s) in relation to the adjoining land and highway(s), and
any other changes proposed in the levels of the site, have been submitted to,
and approved by, the local planning authority.The level details submitted shall
clearly show the proposals in relation to the current levels around the
existing trees and the linkage of the proposed levels to the existing levels of
the surroundings outside the development site.

Foul Water DisposalThe development hereby permitted in relation to
the Detailed Application and the Outline Application shall not commence
(excluding any demolition or site clearance work), until details of the
disposal of sewage for each relevant phase of the development have been
submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.The development shall be carried out in
accordance with the details as so agreed and retained thereafter.

Disposal of Surface WaterThe development hereby permitted in relation to
the Detailed Application and the Outline Application shall not commence
(excluding any demolition or site clearance work) until details of the disposal
of surface water, including surface water attenuation, for each relevant phase
of the development, have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local
planning authority.The development shall be carried out in
accordance with the details as so agreed and retained thereafter.

out in accordance with the strategy agreed and shall be retained as such

Car Park
Design and Management PlanPrior to the commencement of works on the
internal loop road of the detailed phase of the development hereby permitted, a
Car Parking Design and Management Plan shall be submitted to, and agreed in
writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall set out the following: a)    Details of spaces that are to be 'active' electric vehicle charging

provision of one active Electric Vehicle Charging Point for at least 20% of

converting passive provision to active should demand increase.b)    Mechanism for increasing the number of spaces that have an 'active'
electric vehicle charging point if monitoring demonstrates additional demand. c)    Details of the allocation and management of the disabled car parking
spaces.d)    Details of monitoring, management and enforcement procedures for parking
within the site.e)    Details of future provision of disabled person’s parking spaces should
demand increase including f)     A plan showing an updated provision of disabled car parking spaces to
demonstrate a minimum of 3% provision from the outset of occupation, with the
potential provision of a minimum additional 3% additional disabled car parking
spaces (or other amount to be agreed by the LPA), taking into account the
location of wheelchair accessible housing (and demonstrating compliance with
relevant building regulations, legislation and policy) The plan shall be implemented in
accordance with the agreed details and thereafter retained unless otherwise
agreed in writing by the local planning authority.
